name: entity-seo
works_with: Claude Code, or as a plain Markdown playbook
short: Maps you, your brand, company and products as linked entities, then helps your site, schema and profiles describe those links the same way.
what: An entity SEO skill that lists your entities, writes down why each link between them exists and saves it all in one `entities.yaml` file. It then runs separate actions: audit, on-site fixes like a JSON-LD graph and a page per entity, copy for your profiles, articles, measurement and an optional report. It also covers on-site SEO, GEO and AEO, and ships free scripts for Search Console rank and Knowledge Graph checks.
who: Individuals and companies whose name, brand and products don't line up in search, or who get outranked by someone with the same name. It promises no rankings.
needs: Claude Code, or just read the Markdown files
For the optional scripts: Python 3, `google-auth`, a Search Console service account key and a Knowledge Graph Search API key

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: The folder name becomes the skill name. For a team, put it in `<repo>/.claude/skills/entity-seo/` and commit it.

steps.title: Restart your agent
steps.text: Restart Claude Code, or reload, so it picks up the skill.

steps.title: Run it
steps.text: With no argument it picks the next action. Or name one, like `/entity-seo map` or `/entity-seo audit`. It asks for your name, domain and profiles first and asks you to confirm the map before changing anything.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Do entity SEO for me and my company.

watch: The `site` action changes your codebase. It asks you to confirm the entity map first.
The optional scripts need a Search Console service account key and a Knowledge Graph API key. The README says to keep them `chmod 600` and out of git.
No guarantees on rankings, and the README says results take weeks.
